mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand measured by HOUST coincides with stronger S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as investors anticipate future earnings growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with HOUST changes (p > 0.05) in a 60-day rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment as indicated by PAYEMS leads to increased consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite a one-standard-deviation increase in PAYEMS over the prior 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand or supply chain issues, which typically precede short-term S&P 500 declines over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a baseline of stable INDPRO (p > 0.1) in a 200-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4%, the expected discount rate increase dampens future equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 4% for at least 30 consecutive days.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST and RSAFS together indicate strengthening demand, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days when both signals persist.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significant after controlling for individual HOUST and RSAFS effects (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% suggests tighter labor market conditions and can trigger a short-term S&P 500 rally over the next 5 days as investors position for rate cuts.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite UNRATE falling by 0.5 percentage points over the prior 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained decline in GDPC1 (quarterly GDP) by over 2%, the S&P 500 often exhibits negative forward returns over the next 20 days as market anticipates economic weakness.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of stable GDP growth (p > 0.1) in a 40-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains unchanged for three consecutive months in a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 shows higher forward returns over the next 60 days as investors interpret stability as a pause before further hikes.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the pause signal in a 200-day historical context.
